title: Praepositiōnēs Fundāmentālēs
subtitle: Praepositiōnēs cum cāsū fīxō (ἐν, εἰς, ἐκ, ἀπό, σύν, πρός) et praepositiōnēs cum sēnsū variante secundum cāsum (διά, μετά, ὑπό).
objectives: Recitāre sex praepositiōnēs commūnēs cum cāsū fīxō ūnicō (ἐν+dat., εἰς+acc., ἐκ+gen., ἀπό+gen., σύν+dat., πρός+acc.)
Explicāre logicam generālem: genetīvus post praepositiōnem saepe significat “ā/ex”, datīvus significat locum statūrium, accūsātīvus significat mōtum versus
Distinguere sēnsūs dīversōs eiusdem praepositiōnis secundum cāsum sequentem (διά, μετά, ὑπό)
Trānsferre phrasēs praepositiōnālēs simplicēs correcte, attendendō semper cāsum

content.intro: Praepositiō Graeca — sīcut Latīna — regit cāsum nōminis sequentis; sed discrīmen praecipuum ā Latīnō est: multae praepositiōnēs Graecae mūtant sēnsum secundum cāsum quem regunt, nōn sōlum sēnsum secundum ipsam praepositiōnem. Attendere cāsum est ergō omnīnō necesse ad sēnsum correctum legendum, nōn sōlum ad grammaticam correctam scrībendam.
content.explanation: Logica generālis (ūtilis ut mnēmonicum, nōn rēgula absolūta): genetīvus post praepositiōnem saepe indicat origine/sēparātiōnem (“ā/ex”, unde vēnit āctiō); datīvus indicat locum statūrium vel īnstrūmentum (“in, cum”, ubi vel quō īnstrūmentō āctiō fit); accūsātīvus indicat mōtum versus vel extēnsiōnem (“ad, per”, quō āctiō tendit). Haec logica nōn explicat omnem cāsum omnis praepositiōnis, sed adiuvat memoriam.

rules.heading: a) Praepositiōnēs cum Cāsū Fīxō
rules.body:
PraepositiōCāsusSēnsusExemplum
ἐνDat.in, apud (locus statūrius)ἐν τῇ πόλει
εἰςAcc.in, ad (mōtus versus)εἰς τὴν πόλιν
ἐκ (ἐξ)Gen.ē, ex (mōtus ā)ἐκ τῆς πόλεως
ἀπόGen.ā, ab (sēparātiō)ἀπὸ τῆς οἰκίας
σύνDat.cum (comitātus)σὺν τοῖς φίλοις
πρόςAcc.ad, versusπρὸς τὴν πόλιν

Nōtā ἐν vs. εἰς: ambae trānsferuntur saepe “in” Latīnē, sed ἐν (+ dat.) est locus STATUS (“in urbe [iam]”), εἰς (+ acc.) est mōtus VERSUS (“in urbem [euntem]”) — discrīmen exāctē analogum discrīminī Latīnō “in” + ablātīvō vs. “in” + accūsātīvō!

rules.heading: b) Praepositiōnēs cum Sēnsū Variante: διά, μετά
rules.body:
Praepositiō+ Genetīvus+ Accūsātīvus
διάper (spatium/tempus): διὰ τῆς πόλεως “per urbem”propter, ob (causa): διὰ τὸν φόβον “propter timōrem”
μετάcum (comitātus): μετὰ τῶν φίλων “cum amīcīs”post (tempus/locum): μετὰ τὴν μάχην “post pugnam”

rules.heading: c) Ὑπό: Trēs Cāsūs, Trēs Sēnsūs
rules.body: ὑπό + genetīvus = “ab” (agēns passīvus, iam vīsum in lēctiōne priōre): λύεται ὑπὸ τοῦ δεσπότου “solvitur ā dominō”. ὑπό + datīvus = “sub” (locus statūrius, rārior in prōsā, frequentior in poēsī): ὑπὸ τῷ δένδρῳ “sub arbore”. ὑπό + accūsātīvus = “sub” (mōtus versus): ὑπὸ τὸ δένδρον “sub arborem [euntem]”. Eadem logica ac ἐν/εἰς: datīvus = status, accūsātīvus = mōtus.

examples: οἱ πολῖται ἐν τῇ πόλει μένουσιν. — Cīvēs in urbe manent. (ἐν + dat., status)
οἱ στρατιῶται εἰς τὴν πόλιν βαίνουσιν. — Mīlitēs in urbem eunt. (εἰς + acc., mōtus)
ἥκομεν ἐκ τῆς οἰκίας. — Venimus ē domō. (ἐκ + gen., orīgō)
διὰ τὸν πόλεμον φεύγομεν. — Propter bellum fugimus. (διά + acc., causa)
μετὰ τὴν μάχην ἐπανερχόμεθα. — Post pugnam revertimur. (μετά + acc., tempus)
βαίνει σὺν τοῖς φίλοις πρὸς τὴν ἀγοράν. — It cum amīcīs ad forum. (σύν + dat.; πρός + acc.)

commonMistakes.wrong: Cōnfundere ἐν (+ dat., status) cum εἰς (+ acc., mōtus), adhibendō ūnam prō alterā indiscrīminātim.
commonMistakes.right: Attendere semper: ἐν indicat “ubi [iam]”, εἰς indicat “quō [euntem]” — discrīmen praecīsē analogum Latīnō in+abl. vs. in+acc.
commonMistakes.why: Discrīmen status/mōtūs est fundāmentāle in syntaxī Graecā praepositiōnum, saepe neglēctum ab incipientibus.

commonMistakes.wrong: Trānsferre διά vel μετά semper eōdem modō, sine attendere cāsum sequentem.
commonMistakes.right: Vidēre cāsum PRIMUM, deinde ēligere sēnsum correctum: διά+gen. “per”, διά+acc. “propter”; μετά+gen. “cum”, μετά+acc. “post”.
commonMistakes.why: Errāre hīc mūtat sēnsum tōtīus sententiae, nōn sōlum stylum — “per urbem” ≠ “propter urbem”.

commonMistakes.wrong: Crēdere ὑπό significāre sōlum “sub”, ignōrandō sēnsum “ab” (agēns passīvus) cum genetīvō.
commonMistakes.right: Recordārī ὑπό + genetīvus in cōnstrūctiōne passīvā semper significat “ab”, nōn “sub”.
commonMistakes.why: Sēnsus “ab” (agēns) est ūsus frequentissimus ipsīus ὑπό in prōsā classicā, magis quam sēnsus locālis “sub”.

items.explanation: Ἐν semper regit datīvum, indicāns locum statūrium.

items.prompt: Quod discrīmen distinguit ἐν ab εἰς?
options: ἐν regit genetīvum, εἰς regit datīvum
items.explanation: Discrīmen est status vs. mōtus, sīgnātum etiam per cāsum (dat. vs. acc.).

items.prompt: Quid significat ὑπό + genetīvus in cōnstrūctiōne passīvā?
items.explanation: Ὑπό + gen. in cōnstrūctiōne passīvā indicat agentem: “ab”.

exercises.title: Ēlige Cāsum Rēctum
exercises.instructions: Ēlige fōrmam rēctam secundum praepositiōnem et sēnsum datum.

exercises.title: Vērum an Falsum
exercises.instructions: Dēcerne utrum vērum an falsum sit.

items.statement: Ἐν et εἰς sunt synōnyma perfecta, intercambiābilēs sine mūtātiōne sēnsūs.
items.explanation: Falsum: ἐν indicat status, εἰς indicat mōtum — discrīmen reāle et significāns.

items.statement: Διά potest significāre “per” (spatium) AUT “propter” (causa), secundum cāsum sequentem.
Πρός semper regit accūsātīvum in omnī ūsū.
items.explanation: Falsum: πρός potest regere etiam genetīvum vel datīvum in sēnsibus rariōribus; accūsātīvus est ūsus praecipuus/frequentissimus hīc discitus.

items.statement: Ὑπό + datīvus significat “sub” (locum statūrium), rārius in prōsā.
items.explanation: Corrēctum: sēnsus locālis cum datīvō exsistit sed est minus frequēns quam ὑπό+gen. (agēns).

summary: Cāsū fīxō: ἐν+dat. (in, status), εἰς+acc. (in, mōtus), ἐκ+gen. (ē/ex), ἀπό+gen. (ā/ab), σύν+dat. (cum), πρός+acc. (ad).
Logica generālis: genetīvus = orīgō/sēparātiō, datīvus = status, accūsātīvus = mōtus versus.
Attendere semper cāsum post praepositiōnem: sēnsus tōtīus phrāsis inde pendet, nōn sōlum grammatica.
